body: Customer communication scripts
What can we say to help a customer?
Read, choose, say or write.
stages.notes: Untimed. Introduce four customer situations and the script card. Source: sources/MTP.xlsx; revision sha256:0895674f2901b602daf998b8a7aa1516522ce0c301b23bfba941fcc1807977cd. Medium Term Plan!C8; Lesson register!F10.

stages.title: Arrival task
body: Name one product and one service.
What does polite mean?
A customer mentions an allergy. What do you do?
Why repeat an order back?
BLUE / GREEN / AMBER / RED. Choose a pause or quiet station.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer a brief pause, quiet breathing or a quieter station without requiring a public colour disclosure. Agree one return action privately. Expected: drink as a product, taking an order as a service; words/actions showing care; pause and ask the responsible adult to check approved allergen information; repeating helps detect a wrong drink or amount. Never guess, advise a substitute or assure safety. Individual stations. An adult is the customer and observer. No pair work, cold calling or performance in front of the class. Adults may read, rephrase or scribe the learner’s exact words; they record the help and do not choose the learner’s assessed lines, decisions or tips. A model, blank form or planned duration is not completed individual evidence.

stages.title: Which greeting helps?
body: A: What do you want? Hurry up.
B: Hello. Welcome. How can I help you?
Which greeting would make you come back? Why?
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Adult reads both lines with a calm voice. Expected B: it welcomes and invites the customer to speak. A different pace or communication method is valid; do not judge accent, eye contact or performance style.

stages.title: Today I can
body: Build a service script for greeting, taking a drink order, booking a room and handling a complaint.
I can choose a useful line for each situation.
I can check an order and booking details.
I can rehearse quietly with an adult.
stages.notes: Untimed. Exact supplied outcome. [QUAL] — planner mapping. Short I-can lines are local classroom checks, not official criterion quotations.

stages.title: Four useful script lines
body: Greet: Hello. How can I help you?
Order: One tea and one water. Is that right?
Booking: Guest code, date and nights. Is that right?
Complaint: I am sorry. Tell me what went wrong.
Listen. Offer an agreed fix. Refer when needed.
stages.notes: 5 minutes. Model all four situations with the adult using the model cards. For booking use the fictional Guest A, 14 June, two nights and check all three details. For complaint listen, apologise, offer to ask the responsible adult about a replacement, then refer; do not promise a refund or an unauthorised fix. These are paper-based training role plays. Do not prepare or serve real food or drinks, make a real booking, take payment or use personal customer details. Use the fictional guest codes and practice dates only. An allergy question means pause the order and ask the responsible adult to check the approved allergen information; never guess or promise a food is safe. A spill is discussed only: pause, keep clear and alert the adult. Follow the setting’s agreed safety procedures for any real incident.

rows: Hello. Welcome. How can I help you?
One tea and one water. Is that right?
May I check: Guest A, arrival 14 June, two nights. Is that right?
I am sorry. Please tell me what went wrong. I can ask the responsible adult about a replacement.

stages.title: Build the script together
body: Choose one line we can use for each situation.
What must we repeat in a drink order?
Which three details do we check for a room?
How can we respond to a complaint calmly?
stages.notes: 5 minutes. Co-create four short lines on the board. Expected order: drink names and amounts; booking: guest code, practice check-in date and nights; complaint: listen, apologise, offer an agreed next step and refer. Hinge: “I did not hear the drink, so I will guess.” Correct response: ask again and confirm. A shared model is a scaffold, not the learner’s completed individual evidence.

body: Keep your four-situation script and rehearsal record.
Check one line you want to improve.
Record the help you used.
I improved __.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. File VOC3-L1-E1 and E2 using the evidence app under the approved workflow. Keep actual date, duration, observation and initials blank until taught. Record actual contribution; no challenge-completion or earned-time tick is automatic.

stages.title: Exit ticket
body: Adult gives you a short drink order.
Repeat it back accurately.
Ask: Is that right?
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Use a new order from the same training menu, such as one orange juice and one water. Accept a clear spoken, signed or supported communication response. Check exact drink names and amounts; do not assume a neat written script proves accurate communication.

stages.title: Key words
body: Greet: welcome politely.
Order: what the customer asks to buy.
Booking: arrange a room or service.
Confirm: check the details are right.
Complaint: a report that something is wrong.
Apologise: say you are sorry.
Refer: ask a person who can help.
stages.notes: Untimed vocabulary reference. Use the exact practical examples and repeat a phrase before asking for a definition. No personal experience disclosure is needed.

Build four short service lines, then rehearse greeting and order-taking quietly with the adult. This return contains two vocational lessons only; the separate Careers digital-footprint lesson is outside scope.

planner_sections.heading: Timing
paragraphs: Arrival 4; starter 2; I Do 5; We Do 5; You Do 18, split script 12 and rehearsal 6; tidy/file 4; exit 2. Total 40 minutes. Opening, outcome, vocabulary and hidden staff slides are untimed.

planner_sections.heading: Before the lesson
paragraphs: Prepare the training menu, script frames, four three-option MCQs, blank script/rehearsal records and a quiet individual station. Agree how the learner can pause and return. The adult is both customer and observer. No peer acting or whole-class performance is required.

These are paper-based training role plays. Do not prepare or serve real food or drinks, make a real booking, take payment or use personal customer details. Use the fictional guest codes and practice dates only. An allergy question means pause the order and ask the responsible adult to check the approved allergen information; never guess or promise a food is safe. A spill is discussed only: pause, keep clear and alert the adult. Follow the setting’s agreed safety procedures for any real incident.

planner_sections.heading: Modelling and checks
paragraphs: Model greeting, drink order repeated back, room booking with fictional guest code/date/nights, and complaint with listening, apology, an agreed fix and referral. Repeat-back checks accuracy; do not equate communication quality with accent, eye contact or theatrical performance.

Arrival answers: a drink is a product; taking an order is a service; polite words show care; allergy query means pause and refer for approved information; repeat-back catches mistakes. Hinge: ask again rather than guessing an unclear order.

planner_sections.heading: Routes and ownership
paragraphs: Supported uses a script frame. MCQ access chooses the best line from three for each situation and copies or dictates the chosen line. Independent uses own wording. Aspire resolves an order error respectfully.

VOC3-L1-E1 is the individual four-situation script or recorded selections. VOC3-L1-E2 is an actual observed greeting/order rehearsal. Record exactly what was performed and prompted. Do not infer all four role plays were completed in this first rehearsal.

staff_answers: Best-line MCQ answers: greeting B (2); order A (1); booking C (3); complaint B (2). Accept an equally polite and accurate learner-authored line; the model wording is not compulsory.
Order model: one tea and one water; repeat both drink names and amounts and wait for confirmation. A clear supported communication method is valid. Ask again if unclear rather than guessing.

Booking model uses fictional Guest A, arrival 14 June, two nights. Check and repeat the guest code, practice check-in date and nights. These are training details, not a teaching date or a real booking.

Complaint: listen, apologise, offer an agreed next step and refer to the responsible adult if permission or information is needed. Do not argue, blame the customer, promise a refund or make an unapproved replacement.
Allergy query: pause the order and ask the responsible adult to check approved allergen information. Do not guess, recommend a substitute or promise safety. This lesson uses no real food or drinks.
A chosen line or completed script is not proof of a performed rehearsal. Keep the learner’s actual greeting, repeat-back, confirmation, improvement and support record.

model_scripts.customer: Hello. I would like to order a drink.
model_scripts.model_line: Hello. Welcome. How can I help you?
model_scripts.check: A polite greeting, calm voice and time to listen.

model_scripts.customer: One tea and one water, please.
model_scripts.model_line: One tea and one water. Is that right?
model_scripts.check: Repeat the drink names and amounts; wait for confirmation.

model_scripts.customer: Guest A. Two nights from 14 June.
model_scripts.model_line: May I check: Guest A, arrival 14 June, two nights. Is that right?
model_scripts.check: Record the fictional guest code, practice check-in date and number of nights; repeat them back.

model_scripts.model_line: I am sorry. Please tell me what went wrong. I can ask the responsible adult about a replacement.
model_scripts.check: Listen, apologise, offer an agreed next step and refer if needed. Do not argue or promise a refund.

best_line_choices.prompt: A customer has just arrived. Choose the best first line.
options: Hello. How can I help you?
best_line_choices.reason: A polite welcome gives the customer a chance to speak.

best_line_choices.prompt: The customer asks for one tea and one water. Choose the best check.
options: One tea and one water. Is that right?
I will just guess the order.
best_line_choices.reason: Repeat both drink names and amounts, then wait for the customer to confirm.

best_line_choices.prompt: You need to make a training room booking. Choose the best line.
options: There is no need to check.
May I check the guest code, practice check-in date and number of nights?
best_line_choices.reason: These details let you record and confirm the correct fictional booking.

best_line_choices.prompt: The customer says the drink is cold. Choose the best first response.
options: I am sorry. Please tell me what went wrong.
best_line_choices.reason: A calm apology and listening come before the agreed fix or referral.

role_play_scenarios.customer_prompt: Hello. I have not been here before.
role_play_scenarios.expected: Polite greeting, offer of help, listen without interruption.
role_play_scenarios.evidence: Observer records the learner’s own line and support used.

role_play_scenarios.customer_prompt: Order ticket 1: Guest A asks for one tea and one water. Order ticket 2: Guest B asks for two apple juices and one orange juice. Give one order at a time; confirm only after the learner repeats it.
role_play_scenarios.expected: Record and repeat each drink and amount accurately; ask if anything is unclear.
role_play_scenarios.evidence: Two individual order tickets and observer notes.

role_play_scenarios.customer_prompt: Use fictional practice details: Guest C; arrival 18 July; two nights. Confirm only after the learner repeats the details.
role_play_scenarios.expected: Record the fictional guest code, practice check-in date and nights; repeat them for confirmation.
role_play_scenarios.evidence: Training booking form and observer notes. No real booking is made.

role_play_scenarios.customer_prompt: The drink is cold. I would like this put right. Speak calmly. Do not raise the demand or use personal criticism.
role_play_scenarios.expected: Listen, apologise, check the issue, offer a fix within permission and refer to the responsible adult.
role_play_scenarios.evidence: Observer records the learner’s words, proposed action and support used.

tip_choices.text: Repeat the order or booking details and check them.
tip_choices.reason: The customer can correct a mistake before the next step.

tip_choices.text: Guess when you are not sure what the customer said.
tip_choices.reason: Ask for the unclear detail and confirm it instead.

tip_choices.text: Use polite words and listen to the customer.
tip_choices.reason: The customer is heard and can explain what they need.

tip_choices.text: Argue if a customer makes a complaint.
tip_choices.reason: Listen calmly, apologise and seek an agreed next step.

tip_choices.text: Apologise, offer an agreed fix and refer when needed.
tip_choices.reason: The issue can move to a person who can help or authorise a fix.

tip_choices.text: Promise that food is safe without checking.
tip_choices.reason: Pause and ask the responsible adult to check approved allergen information.

deck_notes_template.ta_brief: Read the prompt, offer the agreed route and record support. The learner supplies their choices and wording. The adult plays the customer at the individual station.
